findings.claim: The script uses the BSD/macOS-only `sed -i '' -E` syntax, which fails on GNU sed (Linux). When it fails, the .env update does not happen but the script still prints that GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL was updated.

After the deleteCache mutation in CredentialActionsDropdown succeeds, it only calls onSuccess and does not invalidate viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars. Callers that pass no onSuccess, such as EventAdvancedTab, then show a stale cacheUpdatedAt / 'Last updated'.

SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) is called with empty data. With updateMany in Prisma 5.4.2 this does not bump @updatedAt, nothing reads SelectedCalendar.updatedAt, and the call adds an extra UPDATE on every fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache run.
The cache 'Last updated' timestamp is formatted with a hard-coded `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)`, which ignores the user's locale (i18n.language from useLocale) and profile timezone.
dev:cron switches from ts-node to `npx tsx`, but tsx is not declared as a dependency and is not in yarn.lock. npx therefore downloads it from the registry at run time.
prisma.credential.findFirst has no select, so it loads the full Credential row, including the key (OAuth tokens), only to check existence and ownership.
The mock getCacheStatusByCredentialIds does not accept the credentialIds parameter, so it does not match the interface signature.
